contracts.name: CreateMaterialProperties
contracts.summary: Creates or updates named isotropic material definitions using the source legacy E/G scale.
parameters: mpSet
Non-null, nonempty set without null packets. All input values are snapshotted and validated before the first native call.
contracts.returns: The same Property adapter for fluent chaining after the requested workflow completes.
contracts.remarks: When to use: This legacy compatibility overload multiplies E and the derived G by exactly 1000 and leaves density, thermal expansion and damping unchanged, matching the main source. This is a fixed legacy scale, not a detected unit conversion. Prefer the NoConversion overload after preparing inputs in the acquired native creation convention. Calls CreateIsotropicMaterialProperties: native 0 means Created and 1 Updated, not a material ID. Records LastCreationStatus after success and leaves Id unchanged, correcting the source status-as-ID assignment. General error -1 and other undocumented responses throw without changing that packet's prior status/Id. Earlier successful definitions survive a later failure. G is computed from E/Poisson as in the source packet, not read from native storage. Does not populate assignment sets, assign entities, send Fy/Fu/Ry/Rt/Fcu, save or roll back.

contracts.name: GetAllExtendedIsotropicMaterialProperties
contracts.summary: Reads all extended isotropic material definitions by native zero-based index.
contracts.returns: A new mutable name-equal set of material packets with actual native names and zero-based Id values; empty for a zero inventory. Case-insensitive duplicate names collapse, retaining the first packet.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use to enumerate definitions regardless of their use by supplied entities. Bounds the count to 100000 and uses the existing qualified indexed query for every item, checking its native name, constants and count consistency. Rechecks the total count afterward. Correctly retains returned names instead of leaving every indexed packet unnamed as in the source. Retains native strength values. Compatibility G/K remain derived; use the qualified indexed query to inspect directly observed G. Assignment sets are initially empty. Same-count external edits cannot be ruled out. No native mutation, inferred units or defaults replace failed reads.
contracts.example: foreach (var material in property.GetAllExtendedIsotropicMaterialProperties()) System.Console.WriteLine(material.Name);

contracts.remarks: When to use: Use to enumerate definitions regardless of their use by supplied entities. contracts.name: GetAllExtendedIsotropicMaterialPropertiesWithPopulatedAssignments
contracts.summary: Reads all indexed isotropic definitions and populates candidate assignments.
parameters: forBeams
Optional finite sequence of non-null positive-ID beam candidates; null/empty skips replacing beam assignments.
forPlates
Optional finite sequence of non-null positive-ID plate candidates; null/empty skips replacing plate assignments.
contracts.returns: New material packets with matching original candidate references in Beams/Plates. Definitions are name-equal using the current culture, ignoring case; unknown native entity IDs are not synthesized.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use to include unused definitions as well as assigned materials. Retrieves all indexed isotropic materials first. Uses extended strength reads. Snapshots each input sequence once, validates candidate IDs, and stages all native assignment reads before updating packet sets. Native material subset count/list contracts and the 100000-entry limits apply. Null/empty candidate sides leave that side unchanged. The typed single-material APIs retain their qualified return packets; compatibility collection methods map those observations into mutable MaterialProperty packets. No geometry hydration, native assignment, conversion, save or model-wide atomic snapshot is implied.
contracts.example:
var materials = property.GetAllExtendedIsotropicMaterialPropertiesWithPopulatedAssignments(new[] { new Beam { Id = 17 } }, new[] { new Plate { Id = 17 } });
System.Console.WriteLine(materials.Count);

contracts.signature: HashSet<MaterialProperty> GetAllMaterialPropertiesWithPopulatedAssignments(IEnumerable<Beam> forBeams, IEnumerable<Plate> forPlates, Func<string, MaterialProperty> materialResolver)
contracts.name: GetAllMaterialPropertiesWithPopulatedAssignments
contracts.summary: Resolves distinct entity material names with a caller delegate and populates their candidate assignments.
parameters: forBeams
Optional finite sequence of non-null positive-ID beam candidates; enumerated once.
forPlates
Optional finite sequence of non-null positive-ID plate candidates; enumerated once.
materialResolver

Non-null synchronous callback, invoked once per exact distinct discovered native name on the caller apartment under this adapter's reentrant lock. Must return a non-null packet with a nonblank Name. Its returned Name selects native assignment lookups; it may deliberately resolve an alias.
contracts.returns: A mutable set of the resolver-returned original material packets, deduplicated by their current-culture case-insensitive names, with staged assignment subsets populated.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use for custom material resolution/caching without recreating packets. Does not itself query constants; the callback decides how they are obtained. Native name discovery must succeed before resolution. A callback exception propagates. All assignment reads complete before any returned packet assignment set is changed; nonempty candidate sides clear/repopulate the existing sets (or initialize null sets), while null/empty sides preserve them. Native and callback side effects cannot be rolled back. Do not rename packets already stored in sets. No save, unit conversion or entity assignment occurs in this helper.
contracts.example:
var materials = property.GetAllMaterialPropertiesWithPopulatedAssignments(new[] { new Beam { Id = 17 } }, new[] { new Plate { Id = 17 } }, name => new MaterialProperty(name));
System.Console.WriteLine(materials.Count);

contracts.name: CreatePlateThicknessProperties
contracts.summary: Creates uniform native thickness definitions from scalar thickness packets.
parameters: ptSet
Non-null nonempty set of non-null packets with finite positive Thickness values in the acquired native creation length convention. All values are copied before native access.
contracts.returns: The same Property adapter for fluent chaining after the requested workflow completes.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use for one uniform scalar thickness per definition; use PlateElementThickness creation for explicit four-corner values. Preserves the source scalar CreatePlateThicknessProperty route. Stores only a positive returned native definition ID; invalid/error responses throw and retain that packet's prior ID. Does not assign plates, convert units or save. Earlier successful creations survive later failure.

contracts.returns: The same Property adapter for fluent chaining after the requested workflow completes.

contracts.name: CreateAndAssignOffsetSpecifications
contracts.summary: Groups managed member-end offsets, creates native definitions and assigns their target members.
parameters: beams

Non-null set of positive-ID beams. Null StartOffset/EndOffset is ignored. Definition location/frame and components must be valid and finite; packet Location is used as supplied rather than inferred from the Beam property.
contracts.returns: The same Property adapter for fluent chaining after the requested workflow completes.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use to apply populated or manually supplied nonzero offset packets. Groups by exact Location/Axis/X/Y/Z equality, preserving the first packet's existing Beams and adding the supplied beams using equal offsets. Creates all definitions before starting assignments. Copies each positive created ID into all equal source packets and adds candidate references to the canonical packet. Definitions below the 1e-9 per-component zero threshold are skipped in both overloads, avoiding source degree-pipeline assignments of uncreated ID zero. Assigns each grouped ID array. Requires positive creation IDs and integral zero assignment success. Empty beams/no offsets is a no-op. Earlier creations/assignments remain if a later step fails; no cleanup, unit conversion, save or analysis occurs. Do not mutate definition values while held in hash sets.
contracts.example:
var beam = new Beam { Id = 17, EndOffset = OffsetSpecification.GlobalYEnd(-0.15) };
property.CreateAndAssignOffsetSpecifications(new System.Collections.Generic.HashSet<Beam> { beam });

contracts.name: PopulateMemberReleases
contracts.summary: Reads both member-end release specifications into the supplied managed beams.
parameters: forBeams
Non-null finite sequence of non-null positive-ID beams. Equal candidates are queried once; original beam references are updated only after all reads succeed.
contracts.returns: The same Property adapter for fluent chaining after the requested workflow completes.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use before inspecting StartRelease/EndRelease. Calls the checked basic GetMemberReleaseSpec route for each end, preserving the source query choice. Projects Boolean release/spring fields while retaining every native 0/1/-1/-2/-3 mode in NativeSpecification, including mixed modes. Basic reads do not supply separate common/directional extended MP outputs; compatibility zero placeholders are not evidence of native zero. Use the existing extended typed query when those outputs are needed. Does not resolve native specification IDs, create/assign releases, save or convert units. Any read failure leaves all supplied beam release references unchanged.

contracts.name: CreateAndAssignMemberEndReleases
contracts.summary: Creates and assigns basic full-release/spring specifications at supplied member ends.
parameters: beams
Non-null set of non-null positive-ID beams. Null/no-release ends are skipped. Use independent release packets for start and end; applicable spring inputs must be finite and nonnegative.
contracts.returns: The same Property adapter for fluent chaining after the requested workflow completes.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use for the source basic 0/1 release-flag and six-spring workflow. Snapshots all end requests before the first native write and rejects common/directional partial-moment packets with NotSupportedException rather than silently dropping -2/-3 modes or MP factors. Each end is created with CreateMemberReleaseSpec, its positive ID is stored, then it is assigned to the member using integral-zero AssignMemberSpecToBeam success. Starts precede ends for each supplied beam. Translational springs retain force/length units; rotational springs retain moment/angle units. Native interpretation of combined flags/springs requires live qualification. Does not save, convert units, run analysis, roll back earlier operations or delete orphaned definitions after assignment failure.
